h2: Liquid penetrant testing in the Seattle area: Nadcap shop work versus field PT
html:
Liquid penetrant testing in the Seattle area: Nadcap shop work versus field PT

Penetrant testing around Seattle splits into two kinds of work. Aerospace fluorescent penetrant inspection happens on controlled lines in Nadcap-accredited facilities. Field and shop PT covers stainless, nickel alloy and aluminum welds in refineries, shipyards and fabrication shops. Atlantis works out of Houston and sends crews for field and shop PT. It does not claim Nadcap accreditation for any process line.

What Nadcap penetrant inspection involves. Many searches for "Nadcap liquid penetrant inspection" come from suppliers to Boeing's Renton and Everett plants and to the aerospace machine shops around them. Nadcap is run by the Performance Review Institute. The penetrant audit uses checklist AC7114/1, along with the general NDT criteria in AC7114. Accreditation belongs to the facility that runs the process, not to a traveling crew. It covers the line itself: penetrant materials qualified to AMS 2644, process control to ASTM E1417, the daily system performance checks, the UV-A and white-light readings in the viewing booth, and the written practice behind the inspectors. If a part needs Nadcap-controlled FPI, it goes to an accredited line. Atlantis can still help a supplier prepare. Its outsourced ASNT NDT Level III service writes procedures and written practices and audits them. Where the customer's specification requires NAS 410 Level 3 sign-off, that work is done through an associate.

Field and shop PT around Puget Sound. Outside aerospace, most penetrant work is visible or fluorescent PT on non-magnetic material. In the refineries at Cherry Point, Ferndale, Anacortes and Tacoma, that means stainless and alloy piping welds, exchanger tube-to-tubesheet welds and repair excavations during turnarounds. At Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and in commercial repair yards, it means stainless systems, non-ferrous propeller and shaft components, and weld-repair checks between passes. On naval work, the acceptance standard is NAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 rather than ASME Section V.

Local conditions that affect PT. Puget Sound weather is damp and cool for much of the year, and both affect penetrant work. Most standard procedures qualify penetrant dwell within a set temperature range, so outdoor examinations in winter need warming or a procedure qualified for lower temperatures. Wet surfaces must be dried before the penetrant goes on. Crews should arrive with heating, cover and a procedure that matches the actual site conditions, not the conditions in the brochure.

  • Nadcap FPI: performed on accredited lines under AC7114/1, AMS 2644 and ASTM E1417
  • Refinery stainless and alloy welds, tube-to-tubesheet joints and repair cavities
  • Shipyard stainless and non-ferrous components, including NAVSEA-governed work
  • Cold-weather and wet-surface controls written into the procedure

Routing. Searches for liquid penetrant testing services are answered nationally on penetrant testing. Weld-focused scopes in the city are on weld inspection in Seattle, and the aerospace supply chain is covered on aerospace NDT in Seattle. To train staff in the method, see penetrant testing training and the penetrant simulator. To discuss a field scope or written-practice support, use the Seattle PT enquiry.
